analysis:
Source pass covered only the documentation changes: changelog.d/m5-paged-automatic-concurrency.md (new) and docs/architecture/inference.md (hunk around base lines 97-102). They describe a behavioral change not shown here: on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra, models on the native `auto` paged allowlist default to concurrency 8 (up from 4) when `engine_v2_max_concurrent` is absent. This relies on `ServingPerformanceProfiles.automaticConcurrency` and `EngineV2Bridge.hasPostureGatedWidth`. Chip identity is read from one sysctl, not full hardware detection. The width falls back to the configured width under Low Power Mode or thermal pressure. The coordinator's per-model quality cap, physical KV caps, the shared whole-Mac service allowance and explicit operator settings are stated to remain in force.

No code is in this batch, so I cannot confirm the claimed bounds. Threat IDs for the integration pass to check: T-029 and T-010 (availability and resource monopolization) and T-028 and T-041 (cross-request KV and prefix-cache exposure). Higher concurrency means more tenants' KV and prefix state share GPU memory and more requests share the SSD prefix cache. The documentation says the prefix-cache design and identity are unchanged. A sysctl-based chip check is spoofable only by a provider operator who already controls the machine (ADV-001). The coordinator is not described as trusting that chip claim for authorization.

The actual Swift changes in ServingPerformanceProfile.swift, EngineV2Bridge and ProviderConfig should be checked against the documented fallbacks, the admission and KV reservation limits, and the claim that explicit `4` settings stay unchanged. No security regressions are evident from the docs alone.
